messages:
Julia (sales): Hey team — acme is ramping the POC. They need a hybrid private deployment: on-prem app -> our VPC. Questions: peering vs PrivateLink, failover to hosted API, firewall rules to allow, and any pricing delta we should surface.
Ashley (netops): quick q — do they want source-IP preservation (eg, see client IP) or is SNAT to our EIP ok?
Julia (sales): They insist on preserving source IP on TCP connections for their logging. Also ask for mTLS between their proxy and our endpoint.
Mike (eng): Preserving src IP rules out NAT gateway for egress. For PrivateLink we terminate in customer VPC so src IP is preserved from their side; for our side we still see the VPCE interface IPs. If they need original client IP in our app logs, we typically ask them to forward via X-Forwarded-For at their proxy.
Ian (solutions): To be concrete: two viable architectures — (A) AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints) with our Private deployment in their VPC or partner VPC; (B) VPC peering + NAT/IGW egress with static EIP(s). Each has tradeoffs for failover and IP preservation.
Ashley (netops): For mTLS we can accept client certs at the ingress L7 proxy in Private deployment. If they want mTLS to our hosted API fallback we need a TLS client cert trust list and a config change. It’s doable but will need ent ticket and rotation plan.
Julia (sales): What ports do they need to open outbound from their on-prem to the VPC? Also they asked about automatic failover to hosted if Private capacity is saturated.
Mike (eng): Minimal ports: 443 (HTTPS). If they are doing health checks or heartbeats to a specific port we can add. Example firewall snippet they can use:

```
# allow outbound to Redwood private endpoints
allow tcp any 443 -> 10.20.0.0/22 # replace with assigned CIDR
allow udp any 123 -> 169.254.169.123 # ntp if needed
```

Ashley (netops): Also allow our control plane ranges for management (we’ll provide list): 3.5.10.0/24, 52.11.100.0/24 (example). If they insist on only IP allowlist we will provide a stable set for the duration of the POC, but enterprise customers usually prefer VPC-private connectivity.
Ian (solutions): For failover: we support automatic fallback to the hosted API route but only if the route policy permits and credentials/entitlements match. Note: fallback will change egress IPs and could break their IP-restricted firewall unless we use a Proxy/Bastion in their VPC to funnel requests.
Julia (sales): Pricing — call out differences please. Customer wants monthly estimate if we enable PrivateLink + dedicated capacity burst.
Mike (eng): Pricing notes (high level): PrivateLink + Private deployment = platform + infra fee. Dedicated slice for guaranteed throughput adds a monthly commit. Hosted fallback no extra infra fee but usage-based per-token. I'll share numbers in a follow-up doc (need POC QPS & seq length).
Ashley (netops): One more: if they require client-certificate auth, we’ll need an admin on their side to rotate certs or supply an ACME endpoint. Also update: for src-IP preservation in logs we can add X-Forwarded-For header at their proxy; if they refuse header changes we can negotiate a pass-through TCP mode but that breaks most of our L7 features.
Ian (solutions): Risk items to surface to customer: 1) firewall whitelists vs dynamic hosted IPs, 2) mTLS cert rotation and ops burden, 3) latency variance on fallback, 4) audit/compliance for key material.
Julia (sales): Can someone drop a short checklist I can send them? They want one doc for their security team.
Ashley (netops): Sending quick checklist below — feel free to copy: 

- Connectivity option: PrivateLink preferred for strict isolation; VPC peering supported for same-account VPCs.
- Firewall rules: allow outbound 443 to our endpoint CIDRs; allow control-plane CIDRs (we’ll provide).
- Source IP: preserve via X-Forwarded-For or use pass-through (limits features).
- mTLS: supported; require cert exchange & rotation plan.
- Failover: hosted API fallback available but will use different egress IPs -> update allowlists.
- Ports/Protocols: 443 (HTTPS). Optional: 22 for support sessions if approved.
- Actions: provide your expected QPS, average seq length, and any NAT/EIP constraints.

Ashley (netops): +1: we will provide a signed SLA addendum if they opt for dedicated capacity.
Julia (sales): Perfect — I’ll send this. Any gotchas for on-prem proxies (F5, Palo Alto)?
Mike (eng): For F5/Palo Alto: disable TLS inspection for traffic to Redwood IPs if you need cert pinning. Also ensure SNI passthrough if they have multiple hostnames.
Ian (solutions): I’ll join the customer call Wed 10am PT to walk through options.
DeployBot: Reminder: please attach security questionnaire and entitlement checklist to the thread when available.
Julia (sales): Thanks all. I’ll follow up after the call with exact QPS and requested CIDRs.
Ashley (netops): FYI I already provisioned a temporary CIDR for the POC: 10.20.4.0/24. Will confirm full control-plane list by EOD.
Mike (eng): Noted. If they need persistent EIP-based egress we need a 2-week lead for infra.
Julia (sales): Closing loop — will ping once customer confirms. Thanks!
